Designs new database systems end-to-end — from inception through production — including engine and deployment-model selection, server and storage architecture, multi-cloud infrastructure, and high-availability and disaster-recovery posture. Owns 24×7 production reliability and serves as the final escalation point for major outages, complex performance incidents, and cross-team database 911s. Acts as senior technical authority and subject matter expert across multiple database technologies (SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, DynamoDB, Snowflake) and across AWS and Azure. Sets technical direction for major platform initiatives, including AI-augmented database operations Determines database architecture for new business use cases — including engine selection, deployment model (IaaS vs. PaaS), topology, sizing, integration patterns, and availability targets up to 99.99% (4 nines) — across SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, DynamoDB, and Snowflake. Designs and implements multi-cloud database infrastructure across AWS and Azure, including server, storage, and network architecture tuned for top engine performance. Authors and reviews database infrastructure-as-code (Terraform) for provisioning, configuration management, and lifecycle automation. Oversees the security, integrity, and performance of databases across the production estate — including access controls, encryption at rest and in transit, audit logging, HIPAA-aligned PHI protection, vulnerability management, and database integrity validation. Implements monitoring, observability, and alerting across all database systems and cloud platforms, delegates alert response to team members, and audits incident resolution. Leads complex performance triage and 911 response across product engineering teams. Provides technical leadership for peers and delegates tasks for both major and minor projects. Independently implements and documents enhancement requests. Independently reviews and approves technical design specifications. Designs, audits, and tests high-availability and disaster-recovery architectures engineered to meet 99.99% (4 nines) availability SLAs — including cross-region failover, replication topology, RPO/RTO planning, immutable and air-gapped backup architectures for ransomware protection, point-in-time recovery, and validated restore drills. Serves as final escalation point for database issues escalated by Database Engineers and by partner engineering teams — including production 911 incidents, complex performance investigations, and cross-team database-rooted problems across the full Veradigm engineering organization. Independently owns multiple, concurrent minor or major database platform projects from concept to completion — including requirements gathering, architectural design, implementation, task delegation, schedule creation, deployment, testing, and handoff of the technology solution to the business. Independently owns and is subject matter expert in multiple database technologies and cloud platforms — including SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, DynamoDB, and Snowflake — and across managed (PaaS) and self-managed (IaaS) deployment models on both AWS and Azure. Sets technical direction for AI-augmented database operations, including LLM-assisted design, ML-driven anomaly detection, automated performance tuning, and natural-language operational tooling. Expert knowledge of multiple database engines spanning relational (SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL), document and key-value stores (MongoDB, DynamoDB), and cloud data warehousing (Snowflake), including engine internals, configuration, and operational characteristics under production load. Expert knowledge of database performance monitoring, tuning, and triage at the engine, server, and storage layers across multiple platforms. Expert knowledge of database scripting and automation languages (T-SQL, PowerShell, Python, Bash) and of infrastructure-as-code (Terraform) for database provisioning and lifecycle management. Expert knowledge of multi-cloud database engineering across AWS and Azure, including managed database services (RDS, Aurora, Azure SQL, Cosmos DB, DynamoDB, Snowflake) and self-managed engine deployments on cloud compute. Expert knowledge of database server and storage architecture tuned for engine performance — instance class and CPU/memory profile selection, NUMA awareness, OS-level tuning, IOPS planning, volume type selection, and network architecture. Expert knowledge of designing database systems to high-availability SLAs of 99.99% (4 nines) and above, including cross-region failover automation, replication topology, RPO/RTO planning, ransomware-resilient backup architectures, and recovery validation. Expert knowledge of change management principles and the ability act as a proactive change agent Expert knowledge of project management Working Arrangements Standard work week or as defined by assignment requirements Primarily works in standard office environment or remotely May require after-hours, on-call support and/or holidays On-call and after hours work during peak times including end of month/quarter/year; during this time PTO is limited to meet business needs Travel Up to 10% travel may be required Compensation for this job is subject to market conditions, geographic considerations, the candidate’s unique skills and experience, state and local laws, and budget. review_candidates.title: Cyber Solution Area Lead
review_candidates.description: Job Description Everforth ECS is seeking a Cyber Solution Area Lead to work in our Fairfax, VA office. The Cyber Solution Area Lead (Cyber SAL) will lead the strategy, development, and advancement of our cybersecurity capability across the federal market. This is a company-level leadership role for someone who understands the cyber mission, sees where the market is going, and knows how to translate technical expertise into differentiated offerings, stronger customer relationships, smarter investments, and measurable business growth. You will define what we want to be known for in Cyber, where we can win, what capabilities we should build, and how we turn our best ideas and delivery experience into repeatable solutions that customers value. This is not a traditional P&L, sales-quota, or program-delivery role. It is a high-impact horizontal leadership position for someone who can mobilize expertise across the company and make the whole greater than the sum of its parts. What You’ll Own Shape Our Cyber Strategy and Market Position - Own and govern the direction, priorities, market position, offering portfolio, and capability roadmap for the Cyber Solution Area Build a Portfolio of Cyber Offerings - Transform our expertise into a focused portfolio of named, differentiated, repeatable Cyber offerings Drive Growth - Partner closely with Growth, Account, and technical teams on the customer opportunities that matter most Lead the Cyber Community Across the Company - Lead a cross-company Cyber Core Team bringing together leaders and practitioners from Business Units, Delivery, Growth, R&D, Partnerships, Marketing, and other relevant functions Shape Where We Invest - Own the business and portfolio recommendations for company-funded Cyber R&D, IRAD, reusable solutions, accelerators, and other capability investments Represent Everforth ECS in the Federal Cyber Market - Represent Everforth ECS in customer engagements, industry forums, conferences, panels, partner discussions, and other venues where a strong point of view can strengthen our market position. Who We’re Looking For We are looking for a senior Cyber capability leader who combines technical credibility with proven business acumen . You do not need to be the deepest hands-on engineer in the company. You do need to understand Cyber deeply enough to engage credibly with senior customers, engineers, program leaders, Growth teams, technology partners, and executives—and to know the difference between an interesting idea and a capability that can create real customer and business value. The Strongest Candidates Will Bring a Combination Of Broad fluency across the cybersecurity domain Strong understanding of the federal technology and mission market Experience engaging customers and understanding mission needs Experience supporting growth, capture, solutioning, or strategic pursuits Understanding of how Cyber capabilities are actually delivered on programs Strong judgment around technology and R&D investment Ability to work effectively with technology partners and commercial vendors Strong matrix leadership and the ability to mobilize people across organizational boundaries Executive presence and credibility with senior customers and industry leaders A strong point of view about where the Cyber market is headed—and the curiosity to keep challenging it Why This Role Matters This is an opportunity to do more than manage a portfolio. It is an opportunity to define what Cyber becomes at Everforth ECS . You will have visibility across the company, access to exceptional technical and mission talent, and the ability to influence customer strategy, growth, delivery, partnerships, R&D, and investment. If you are the kind of leader who can see patterns others miss, connect people and capabilities across organizational boundaries, turn expertise into market advantage, and build something that scales well beyond yourself, we want to talk to you. Salary Range: $275,000 - $350,000 General Description Of Benefits Required Skills 10+ years of experience in cybersecurity, technology, or related federal mission environments, including progressively responsible technical or leadership roles. Broad cybersecurity expertise across multiple areas such as Zero Trust, identity and access management, cloud security, network security, cyber operations, vulnerability management, DevSecOps/software security, data protection, and security architecture. Demonstrated experience supporting U.S. Federal Government customers and missions, with an understanding of federal cybersecurity priorities, acquisition environments, and technology modernization challenges. Experience translating customer and mission needs into technical solutions, capabilities, offerings, or strategic initiatives. Demonstrated experience supporting business development, capture, solutioning, strategic pursuits, or customer shaping activities. Experience developing or influencing technology strategies, capability roadmaps, solution portfolios, or investment priorities. Strong understanding of how cybersecurity capabilities are designed, implemented, accredited, operated, and sustained within federal environments. Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional and matrixed teams without direct organizational authority. Ability to communicate complex cybersecurity concepts in terms of mission outcomes, customer value, competitive differentiation, and business impact. Strong executive communication and presentation skills, with demonstrated credibility engaging senior government customers, technical leaders, industry partners, and corporate executives. Demonstrated ability to evaluate emerging technologies and determine whether to build, buy, partner, integrate, or reuse capabilities. Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. Government security clearance appropriate to customer and mission requirements. Desired Skills 15+ years of cybersecurity or federal technology experience, including senior technical, solution, strategy, or capability leadership responsibilities. Existing relationships and demonstrated credibility within the DoD, Intelligence Community, Federal Civilian, or broader federal cybersecurity market. Experience developing and scaling repeatable cybersecurity offerings, intellectual property, accelerators, or managed capabilities across multiple customers or programs. Experience with major federal cybersecurity frameworks and initiatives, including NIST Cybersecurity Framework, NIST 800-53, Risk Management Framework (RMF), Zero Trust architectures, CMMC, and federal cloud security requirements. Technical depth in one or more strategic areas such as Zero Trust, cloud-native security, identity, cyber analytics, AI-enabled cybersecurity, secure software development, threat detection and response, or security automation. Experience identifying, prioritizing, and managing IRAD, R&D, or corporate technology investments based on customer demand and measurable business value. Experience building strategic relationships with cybersecurity technology vendors, hyperscalers, OEMs, startups, and other industry partners. Experience contributing to significant federal captures, proposals, or strategic campaigns and developing technical win themes and differentiated solution strategies. Experience developing reference architectures, reusable delivery patterns, or enterprise cybersecurity standards. Demonstrated thought leadership through industry presentations, panels, publications, working groups, or government/industry forums. Bachelor’s or advanced degree in Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Engineering, Information Technology, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience. Relevant professional certifications such as CISSP, CCSP, CISM, GIAC, AWS/Azure security certifications, or comparable credentials. Active U.S. Government security clearance. #EverforthECS1 ECS Federal LLC is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate or allow discrimination on the basis any characteristic protected by law. Our work powers mission-critical outcomes, strengthens technology partnerships, and creates meaningful opportunities for our people. We are defined by a commitment to excellence in delivery, a culture of innovation, and an environment where talent can thrive and grow.
